title: What would we really have paid and got?

what.name: Question
what.value_plain: Are the fees, slippage, funding and fill rules used in the backtests realistic, and does fixing them flip any verdict?
what.label: OURS

what.name: Scan
what.value_plain: Every fee, slippage and funding constant in backtest/ and research/: 201 hits in 70+ files.
what.label: OURS

what.name: Funding rerun
what.value_plain: Five recent screens rerun with the real signed 8-hour funding instead of a flat 1 basis point (0.01 %).
what.label: SOURCED

what.name: Fee reference
what.value_plain: Deribit taker 0.05 %, maker 0 %; Binance taker 0.05 %, maker 0.02 % (fees.py).
what.label: SOURCED

how: Constants are found by regex and tabulated; funding is swapped for the real series and each screen is rerun (the flat run first reproduces the published numbers). Break-even cost = the round-trip fee at which an arm's average gross result is zero.
window: DEV only, 2022-04-01 to 2024-06-30 (sealed VALIDATION and HOLDOUT windows were not read)

verdict.label: No arm earns even the cheapest realistic fee

why: The funding data was never found (wrong folder), so every screen charged a flat 1 bp to both longs and shorts instead of the real signed rate. Fixing it flips no verdict (largest move +0.018 percentage points).

57 of the 70 files that set a cost define their own constant instead of importing fees.py, so net numbers are not comparable across studies (the same gross trade nets -0.10 % to -0.20 % depending on the file).
Costs, not funding, decide every verdict: the best measured gross edge is +3.6 bp, all-taker Deribit costs 10 bp round trip.
